input.quote: This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000
input.rationale: Section 22.4 already carries two fallback elements verbatim: mutual consent for assignment and a "not unreasonably withheld" standard. It fails the fallback on the successor limb, however. M&I may "freely assign" on a merger, reorganization, sale of all or substantially all assets, stock or securities, or to a successor of the M&I Data Services division, while Customer's only consent-free route is a merger in which Customer is a party and where the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 — so a sale of substantially all assets, or a merger with a smaller acquirer, still needs M&I's consent. No written notice is required for either party's permitted assignment. We therefore made the shortest fallback-level fix: a symmetrical successor carve-out for Customer and a mutual written-notice sentence, leaving the consent machinery for all other assignments untouched (we did not add an affiliate carve-out, which would conflict with the fallback level). We did not pursue the preferred position, which would require deleting M&I's negotiated free-assignment right and adding a competitor bar. On change of control, Section 21.11.B commits M&I to "continue to provide Services" and gives it no termination or re-pricing right (it only caps volume at pre-change levels plus 25%), and Section 11.3 (redacted) is referenced in 11.1 as a Customer termination route excused from the Termination for Convenience Fee, i.e. a Customer benefit; neither is flagged.

A successor assignment requires written notice.

mappings.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Broaden Customer's consent-free successor carve-out in 22.4 and add a mutual written-notice requirement for permitted successor assignments.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We broadened Customer's consent-free carve-out to any successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, removing the $100,000,000 acquirer test that M&I's own free assignment right is not subject to, and added a mutual written-notice requirement. This puts the clause at our fallback position: both parties may assign to a successor on written notice, with all other assignments requiring consent that is not unreasonably withheld.

ops.oldText: (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with
ops.newText: (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with

ops.text: The assigning party shall give the other party written notice of any assignment made under clause (a) or (b) above.
